subject: Extracting factor score for individual cases.

messages.author: 2f095572d08a899f
messages.subject: Extracting factor score for individual cases.
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to extract factor scores ("AUDfactor") for each case (individual cases have their own factor score). 

But I get the error message saying that "Warning: lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negativeWarning: lavaan WARNING: factor scores could not be computed due to at least one negative (residual) variance".  How can I fix this?

Following is the code that I used.

"
mimic.model_m1 <- '
   
   #measurement model
   AUDfactor =~ NA*ADCutStop+ADLargerLonger+ADCraving+ADTimeSpent+ADTolerance+ADReducedActivities+AARoleFailure+AAWithdrawal+ADContinuedUse+AAHazardousUse+AAInterpersonal
   
   #fixed variance
   AUDfactor ~~ 1*AUDfactor
   
   #thresholds
   ADCutStop | th1*t1
   ADLargerLonger | th2*t1
   ADCraving | th3*t1
   ADTimeSpent | th4*t1
   ADTolerance | th5*t1
   ADReducedActivities | th6*t1
   AARoleFailure | th7*t1
   AAWithdrawal | th8*t1
   ADContinuedUse | th9*t1
   AAHazardousUse | th10*t1
   AAInterpersonal | th11*t1

'
fit_m1 <- sem(model = mimic.model_m1, data = dat,
                          ordered=c("ADCutStop","ADLargerLonger","ADCraving","ADTimeSpent","ADTolerance",
                                    "ADReducedActivities","AARoleFailure","AAWithdrawal","ADContinuedUse",
                                    "AAHazardousUse","AAInterpersonal"))

dat$factorscore <-lavPredict(fit_m1)
"

Best,

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: Extracting factor score for individual cases.
parts:
Hi,

The first warning indicates that an element of the (residual) covariance matrix is negative. There are various reasons that may cause this, you can look up to warning in the google discussion group to get an overview of possible reasons (and maybe a solution). Two possibilities are small sample size and/or a misspecified model. Perhaps you could look at the (standardized) results of your models to see where the problem is situated, or try fitting a simpler model. In case of continuous items, I would suggest trying bounded estimation, but I have not tried it myself with categorical indicators, so I am not 100% sure whether it works. Nevertheless, I found the following in the paper regarding bounded estimation (please see https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2021.1982716):  "Another advantage is that the bounds work with any estimator (not just maximum likelihood) and so can also be applied in settings where we have missing data, categorical data, or multilevel data.". 

On what scale are your items measured? I think that once you fixed the issue with the (residual) covariance matrix,  you should be able to calculate factor score.

Best wishes,

Jasper
